_comment: OPS-FRESHNESS-SOURCE-TRUTH-W1 R4.5 — public-shape snapshot for the /verify page. Per the CLAUDE.md public-shape-snapshot rule, but for a PAGE rather than a JSON endpoint: the 'shape' is the set of data-tr-field spans, their committed fallbacks, and which of them a producer re-bakes. A span's COMMITTED literal is public copy — Caddy serves landing/verify.html statically and no-JS readers plus every LLM crawler read the bake, not the hydrated value.
served_from: /var/www/algovault/verify.html (Caddy static). NOT in the Docker image — the Dockerfile COPYs only landing/integrations/, landing/skills.html, landing/integrations.html, landing/Prompt/.
render_source: landing/verify.html (committed) -> rewritten host-side by scripts/snapshot-landing-data.mjs -> cp landing/*.html /var/www/algovault/

drift_canary.cadence_before_this_wave: 0 12 * * 1 (weekly — a 7-day blind window on a row whose notes said CRITICAL)

next_batch_in.rationale: A RELATIVE countdown cannot be correctly baked at any cadence, so it must never gain a manifest row. Hydrated in-browser by verify.html's inline updateNextBatchCountdown() on a 60s interval; inert for crawlers, which is the honest degradation.

erc8004_agent_id.rationale: A STABLE identity, not a clock-dependent metric. Freezing it is correct; the forward-stability guard deliberately does not flag bare integers.

forbidden_committed_literal_shapes._comment: A data-tr-field span may hold one of these ONLY if the snapshot manifest owns the key. Enforced by tests/unit/landing-fallback-forward-stability.test.ts (self-tests both directions).

alarm_contract.MERKLE_PUBLISH_LIVENESS: freshness_source: sot. Measures the PUBLISHER via .batches|max_by(.published_at). tolerance_value 0.5d inside the cadence-coherence band (0.0361, 1.0361). Single-fire — a missed publish IS the incident.
alarm_contract.VERIFY_BAKED_BATCH_COPY_DRIFT: EXACT_ISO_MINUTE, page vs SoT. Guards the daily re-bake. Requires 2 consecutive breaches — the injector self-heals daily, so a one-day transient must not page.
alarm_contract.SNAPSHOT_INJECTOR_HEARTBEAT_FRESH: freshness_source: sot reading the heartbeat FILE (attempt-recency, stamped at job start). tolerance 1.5d with missed_cycles_tolerated: 2.
alarm_contract.RETIRED__VERIFY_LATEST_BATCH_FRESH: Derived its measured value from claim_pattern (a page scrape) while naming the publisher, so it actually measured max(deploy_gap, publish_gap) and had zero discriminating power. Its sot_endpoint/sot_jq were dead config. Reintroducing a page-sourced FRESH row is now impossible: the canary fail-CLOSED rejects any FRESH row lacking freshness_source (exit 3).

consumers: no-JS readers + LLM crawlers (read the committed/baked literal directly)
browsers via landing/js/track-record-proxy.js (latest_batch, latest_batch_n, latest_batch_at, erc8004_agent_id) and verify.html's inline script (next_batch_in)
drift_check_command: LIVE=$(curl -fsS https://algovault.com/api/merkle-batches | jq -r .latest_batch_id); PAGE=$(curl -fsS https://algovault.com/verify | grep -oE 'data-tr-field="latest_batch"[^>]*>#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'); [ "$LIVE" = "$PAGE" ] && echo "OK batch #$LIVE" || echo "DRIFT live=$LIVE page=$PAGE"
drift_check_notes: Run any time AFTER 00:39 UTC on a given day. Before the day's re-bake the served page legitimately holds the previous batch. This is the assertion that failed by 3 batches (#106 vs #109) on 2026-07-28 before this wave.
